facts.answer_text: The most likely pathological mechanism in this case is volume loss (atelectasis) causing ipsilateral shift. This means that the collapse or incomplete expansion of the lung on the same side as the mediastinal shift is the primary cause of the observed changes. Common conditions that can cause this pattern in young patients include pneumonia, atelectasis, and congenital lung abnormalities.
